newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank says Shanghai financially sound.
newsitem.headline: China central bank says Shanghai financially sound.

text.p: The financial situation of Shanghai developed in the first half of 1997 to the satisfaction of the central bank, the People's Bank of China, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

Quoting a report by the central bank's Shanghai branch, Xinhua said Shanghai's bank loans had increased appropriately, government treasury bonds were issued smoothly and the level of financial opening-up was raised in the first half of 1997.
Bank deposits in Shanghai rose by 73.3 billion yuan ($8.8 billion) in the first half of 1997, up 16.1 billion yuan compared with the same period of 1996, Xinhua said official statistics showed.
Bank loans rose 28.3 billion yuan in the first six months of 1997, to 2.7 billion yuan more than the same year-ago period, Xinhua said without further details.
Capitalisation on Shanghai's stock market hit 861.2 billion yuan by the end of June, a surge of 57.2 percent from the beginning of this year, Xinhua said.

Six of the nine foreign banks approved to do local currency business on a trial basis in Shanghai's Pudong development zone had successfully launched their operations in the first half of 1997, Xinhua quoted the central bank report saying.
This had helped ease a shortage of local currency faced by foreign-funded enterprises, it said, but gave no further details.
